Question Choices: A graph approaches y = -2 from both sides as x approaches 0. Find the limit.
Hints: Both one-sided limits agree.|Read the common value.
Solution: A limit describes values at inputs arbitrarily close to the target, excluding the target itself. Changing or leaving undefined the value at that one point does not change a limit. Question Choices: What must be true of the one-sided limits for a finite two-sided limit to exist?
Question Answers: both exist and are equal and finite|they approach the same finite value
Hints: Compare the left and right behavior.|They must approach the same value.
Solution: The notation x->a+ means x>a approaches a; x->a- means x<a approaches a. A finite two-sided limit exists exactly when both one-sided limits exist as the same finite number. Unequal finite one-sided limits give a jump discontinuity, regardless of the function value at a. The one-sided limits must be equal.
